scope.supports: Kernel-checked for arbitrary carriers: an exhibited cut has distinct endpoints, a cut exists on V iff V has two distinct points, no cut exists on a subsingleton, a map carrying the relation into an irreflexive target separates the endpoints and (sharper) such a target exists iff the map separates every related pair; instance-without-law and law-without-instance exist, and the three pointed-relation facts hold. Native: every relation on 0..4 points (65536 at n=4) tabulated by cut data, law, instance and the four related/equal quadrants, and every irreflexive relation, map and target on 1..3 points, all matching closed forms with zero exceptions.
scope.does_not_support: Deriving the law (irreflexivity) from the primitive difference <> or from Real_0: the relation and its law remain supplied data; any selection of a preferred cut or orientation (two orientations exist on two points); infinite carriers beyond the Lean statements; the arity-cost tie-breaker of the source (declared_arity_cost_selects is a decide on a priced toy, not used here); the aggregate local theorem pg_to_sn_and_wdp_route_chain_composition, which is a fixed enumeration.
scope.narrowest_claim: A law-bearing cut (an irreflexive relation with an exhibited pair) exists exactly on carriers with two distinct points, its endpoints are apart, and a map separates the endpoints of every cut it carries into an irreflexive target; the pair of marks alone does not supply the relation or its law.
scope.next_test: Replay the admission-floor model counts on 1..4 points with the declared Real_0 axiom list added as constraints and decide whether any declared axiom forces irreflexivity of the relation, i.e. whether the counts of relations with an exhibited pair but no law drop to zero.
